Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@atlasiahealth.com>

Subject: Post-signature: Implementation expectations & MAP details

Hi Mateo,

Thanks — excited to get moving. Procurement completed signatures earlier today and we want to lock the mutual action plan and a clear post-signature implementation playbook so our engineering, security, and training teams can calendar resources. Two quick asks up front:

1) Can you embed a staged rollout + canary plan (dates, traffic targets, rollback triggers) into the MAP?
2) We need a migration window with expected downtime (or zero-downtime approach) & acceptance tests for cutover.

We also need: SOW (final), runbook, and training curriculum so we can approve internal headcount commitments. Can you share a single consolidated MAP doc and a short checklist we can present to our CTO?

Appreciate a first draft by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Samira
Samira Khan
VP Product Operations | Atlasia Health
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-signature: Implementation expectations & MAP details

Hi Samira — congratulations on the close, and thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a single MAP PDF (Atlasia-MAP-implementation-v1.pdf) that embeds the post-signature execution playbook; I’ve also attached a concise canary checklist and training outline for your review. Highlights below — please confirm the proposed dates so we can lock resources.

Executive summary (high-level):
- Goal: Move Atlasia from trial to production with predictable latency/SLOs and zero-data-loss migration.
- Scope: API generation endpoints + embedding store migration + admin UI auth.

Proposed staged plan (summary timeline):
- Prework / Provisioning (Preflight): Apr 10–16, 2028 — environment provisioning, access, baseline tests, security checklist completed.
- Canary Pilot (small traffic): Apr 17–23, 2028 — 5–10% traffic routed to Redwood canary pool, monitoring window 7 days. Acceptance: error rate under 1% and 95th latency <600ms for three consecutive days.
- Phased Ramp (progressive rollout): Apr 24–May 14, 2028 — 25% → 50% → 75% over three waves; each wave gated by canary metrics and runbook sign-off.
- Migration Cutover (final switch): May 21, 2028 — final data sync, DNS cutover, validation smoke tests. Target: <15m observed customer-impactful interruption; if zero-downtime approach acceptable we’ll use double-write + backfill to avoid interruption (preferred).
- Hypercare & Knowledge Transfer: May 21–Jun 4, 2028 — daily warroom, SLAs measured, handoff docs and training complete.

Canary mechanics & rollback triggers:
- Traffic steering: feature flag + routing rules; initial canary pool on Dedicated capacity.
- Metrics to watch: 5xx rate, request latency P95/P99, token throughput, cache hit ratio, and end-to-end user error reports.
- Immediate rollback triggers: sustained 5xx >0.5% for 10m, P95 latency increase >2x baseline for 30m, or any data integrity issue.

Migration approach options (choose with your infra team):
- Option A (double-write + backfill): zero-downtime, recommended.
- Option B (short maintenance window): scheduled 30–60 minutes during off-peak — we’ll provide step-by-step operations.

Training plan (outline):
- Train-the-trainer sessions Apr 18–20 (internal super-users)
- Full user training Apr 25–May 12 (recorded + live Q&A)
- Ops runbook walkthrough Apr 16 and a dry-run Apr 21

Deliverables attached: Atlasia-MAP-implementation-v1.pdf, atlasia-canary-checklist.xlsx, atlasia-training-outline.docx. I’ve also uploaded the MAP to a shared drive (link at the bottom) and sent the final SOW to DocuSign (SOW-Atlasia-Redwood-2028.pdf).

Open asks for you:
- Confirm the preferred migration approach (double-write vs maintenance window).
- Can you nominate an Atlasia migration SME and a training owner by Apr 12?
- Approve proposed initial canary window (Apr 17–23) or suggest a narrower window.

If that timeline works I’ll create the mutual action checklist with weekly owners and add acceptance gating to the HubSpot deal record.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature: Implementation expectations & MAP details

Thanks Mateo — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Can we shorten the canary pilot to Apr 17–20 (4 days)? Our ops window for a larger test cohort is limited. If we do that, we’ll expect a slightly higher confidence bar per day (e.g., <0.5% errors and P95 <550ms).
- We prefer the double-write approach if Redwood can guarantee backfill guidance and final reconciliation checks. Please add the detailed backfill steps to the runbook.
- Training owner: I’ll nominate Jordan Price as Atlasia training lead by EOD Apr 12. Migration SME will be assigned from infra (I will confirm by Apr 12 as well).

We’ll countersign the SOW in DocuSign once we align the MAP dates. Could you compress the preflight checklist into a one-page summary we can share with our CTO?

Samira
